protagonist.who: You are the talk of the pair: an ex-soldier who left the regiment with a bent medal, a bent conscience, and a way of selling a man his own surrender before it happened.
protagonist.history: You and your partner came out of the same border campaign, where you talked the post into surrender and he held it with a broken sword; the contract in the pine clearing is the first time either of you has tried to make a country instead of a camp.
protagonist.wants: to cross the frontier and make yourselves kings of the country no Englishman has seen, so the con becomes a throne
protagonist.need: to find out whether the partnership that made you both can survive the crown, or whether the crown will turn you into two men who only ever shared a tent
protagonist.can_do: bluff, bargain, arrange posts, speak to councils, lead a handful of soldiers into danger, and sign a contract in dirt
protagonist.cannot_do: make the mark's council accept a king without the council's seal, or make the partner share the crown if he has decided the crown is one head and one sword

ties.what: the soldier who thinks a king is made by a sword and an oath, not a sale, and who will follow you into the capital only as long as the contract says you are equals
the old chief of the border posts, who sees through your con and is still charmed by the shape of it, and who holds the seal that can make you kings or strangers
the sergeant who follows you because you led men out of a trench, not because you sold him a kingdom, and who is the bridge between your soldier's past and your king's future

protagonist.open: whether you keep the partnership whole or spend it to get the crown
protagonist.name: Bedwyr Ravel

arena.description: The frontier country from the pine clearing at the border to the capital at the river junction: a chain of trading posts, fords, council lodges, and the road that connects them.

pressure.description: The mark's council will only crown a king at the next river crossing, and the posts are splitting into factions that will each take a different side of the border if they do not get a single head to answer to.
pressure.clock_or_stock: none tracked; the crossing is told through the state of the posts and the river, because 3-0c names no failure

opposition.who_or_what: the mark and the council of traders who guard the posts
opposition.wants: to keep the border posts from splitting and to keep the choosing power in their own hands, even if that means crowning a king they do not quite believe in
opposition.means: they control the seal, the river fords, the traders, and the soldiers who guard the posts; they can name a rival, withhold the crossing, or break the contract by taking back the weapons it was signed with
opposition.shown_by: at the first ford, the mark's people take your sword and the partner's knife and set them on the council stones, saying no man is a king until his weapons are left where the posts can break them

events.what: At the first campfire in the pine clearing, the partner cuts his palm and signs the contract in ash and blood, setting the terms of your shared ambition and making the first real cost of the con.

The mark's council holds an audience in the chief's lodge, where they present a false claim to the border posts and force you and the partner to stand before them as if you were already kings, using charm and threat to convince them to hand over their authority.

At the capital you have just claimed, the con threatens to unravel when the mark's council demands that only one of you take the crown, and you must decide whether to save the partnership or the crown, resulting in a physical or emotional break.

mediation.question: Do you make one king and spend the other, or do you make yourselves kings by keeping the contract equal?

to_reach_pole_a.pole: sovereign ambition: the crown is secured by spending the partnership: one of you takes the throne and the other takes the cost
to_reach_pole_a.what_you_must_do: at the crisis in the capital, take the mark's seal from the council table, set it beside the contract, and hand the partner the contract's price, the name of the country, so he becomes keeper of the contract while you keep the seal and the choosing power
to_reach_pole_a.cost: the partnership is broken, and the one who does not take the crown becomes the keeper of the contract, no longer equal

to_reach_pole_b.pole: shared loyalty: the partnership stays whole: you and the partner divide the crown so neither is alone
to_reach_pole_b.what_you_must_do: from the first ford to the crown in the capital, keep the contract whole by letting each of you hold one half of the crown's work: you take the council's word and the seal, he takes the posts' arms and the soldiers, and neither of you takes the other's burden alone, even when the mark's council demands a single head
to_reach_pole_b.cost: you must give up the chance to be the only king, and the partner must accept that his sword is not enough to make him alone

levers: the contract signed in ash and blood in the pine clearing
the mark's seal, which can make you kings or strangers
the partner's sword, which he believes should be the one that makes the king
the enforcer's loyalty, which is to the soldier, not the con

price.what: the partnership itself: the bond that made you both is traded for the crown, and the one who does not take the throne becomes the keeper of the contract, no longer equal
price.who_pays: you and the partner, whichever of you does not take the crown
price.why_final: the contract was signed in dirt and blood, and once the crown is set, the terms cannot be broken without breaking the man who signed them

setups.plant: at the first campfire, the partner signs the contract in ash and blood, and the mark's people take your sword and his knife and set them on the council stones
setups.payoff: at the crisis in the capital, the mark's council demands that only one of you take the crown, and the weapons on the council stones become the proof that the contract can be broken by taking back what was signed with them

rules.thing: the contract signed in the pine clearing
rules.terms: what is sworn in the clearing binds both of you until the crown is set; if one takes the crown, the other may claim the price named in the contract
the seal may be given to a man who has never held it, but the sword must be carried by the man who will bear the cost; if the sword is carried by one, the crown follows the sword, not the seal

turns.situation: In the pine clearing, the partner has cut his palm and signed the contract in ash and blood, and the mark's scout has brought word that the council will not crown a king at the river crossing unless the king's weapons are left on the council stones first.
turns.what_you_must_do: find out what the council means by a king's weapons, before you and the partner reach the first ford

ways_through.way: it comes out from the mark, when you let her read the contract aloud by the fire, that the weapons are the proof a king will answer the posts, and the council will take your sword and the partner's knife only until the crossing
ways_through.cost: the partner hears the council's words and asks what a king does with a sword he cannot carry, and the contract is now known to the mark before you have sold it to her

ways_through.way: it comes out from the enforcer, who has guarded posts before, that the council stones are a test: a man who leaves his weapon is a man who can be broken by the posts, and a man who keeps it is a man the posts must kill
ways_through.cost: the enforcer tells you by the fire, so the partner does not hear, that he will follow the sword, not the seal

turns.set_piece: the first campfire in the pine clearing, the contract signed in ash and blood, the partner's palm still red

turns.situation: The mark's council holds you and the partner in the chief's lodge, a false claim to the border posts unrolled before you, and the council will not let you leave the lodge until you stand as if you were already kings.
turns.what_you_must_do: get the council to hand over the mark's seal for the road to the capital

ways_through.way: you get the seal because you let the mark speak first and then answer her false claim with the partner's sword laid across the table, so the council sees the posts will be held whether they like it or not
ways_through.cost: the partner has taken the sword out of your hand and made it his argument, and the council hears him as the king, not the partner

ways_through.way: you get the seal because you give the council the name of the country and let them write it into the claim, so the posts become theirs as much as yours
ways_through.cost: the contract in your pocket now names a country the council can take back, and the partner says the words like a man signing his own discharge

turns.set_piece: the audience in the chief's lodge, you and the partner standing before the power-brokers as if already kings, the false claim spread on the table

turns.situation: At the river crossing, the mark's soldiers have closed the ford, and the enforcer's men are on the wrong side of the water with the contract and the seal.
turns.what_you_must_do: hold the ford long enough for the enforcer's men to bring the seal and the contract across

ways_through.way: you hold it because you take the partner's sword and stand in the water with the enforcer, so the men see the king's talk and the soldier's blood in the same body
ways_through.cost: your arm is cut by the council's soldiers, and the partner is left holding the seal while you are the one who bleeds for the crossing

ways_through.way: you hold it because you let the enforcer command the crossing and stand back to sell the council a treaty for the ford
ways_through.cost: the enforcer's men cross whole, but the enforcer has taken the soldiers' loyalty from you, and the partner watches you talk while his sword waits on the council stones

turns.set_piece: the ford under the council's fire, the enforcer's men crossing while you stand in the water with the partner's sword

turns.situation: At the capital you have just claimed, the mark's council fills the room with new allies and old enemies and demands that only one of you take the crown; the weapons on the council stones are the proof that the contract can be broken by taking back what was signed with them.
turns.what_you_must_do: settle who carries the sword into the crown room before the council can name a rival

ways_through.way: the crown is set with both of you, because you take the seal and the partner takes the sword, and the mark gives the seal to the man who has never held it while the sword is carried by the man who will bear the cost
ways_through.cost: the council accepts two kings only because you let the mark keep the choosing power, and the partner's sword is the one that makes the kingdom his as much as yours

ways_through.way: the crown is set with one king, because you take the crown and give the partner the contract's price, the name of the country, so he becomes the keeper of the contract and you the king
ways_through.cost: the partnership is broken, and the enforcer follows the partner's sword out of the room, leaving you the crown and the empty throne

turns.set_piece: the crisis in the capital, the room filled with new allies and old enemies, the council demanding one king, the contract and the seal on the table

complications.description: The enforcer has kept the contract's original terms in his shirt, and when the council tries to rewrite them at the lodge, he will read them aloud only to the man holding the sword.
The mark's seal is not one stone but two halves, one for the council and one for the crossing, and the partner has been carrying the council's half since the pine clearing without telling you.
The council's soldiers have taken the partner's knife from the council stones and kept it in their own belt, so the contract's price can be claimed with a weapon the partner no longer has.

cast_seeds.wants: to keep the border posts unified under the council's seal, not a single king's sword
cast_seeds.holds: the seal that legitimizes the crown and the council's authority over the fords
cast_seeds.edge: sees through the con but is charmed by the elegance of the performance, so he tests you rather than breaking you
cast_seeds.tie: holds the seal that can make you kings or strangers, and remembers the old days when soldiers were just men in the mud
cast_seeds.voice: speaks in riddles wrapped in legalities, treating your ambition as a business transaction: 'A king without a seal is just a man with a loud voice. Show me the silence in your hand.'
cast_seeds.name: Rook Underhay

cast_seeds.wants: to be recognized as the equal half of the kingdom, not the sword in the con artist's hand
cast_seeds.holds: the contract signed in blood and the respect of the soldiers who follow him
cast_seeds.edge: believes a king is made by a sword and an oath, not a sale, and resents the need to share the glory with the man who talked his way out of the trench
cast_seeds.tie: shared the tent and the broken sword with you, and expects the contract to mean what the blood said
cast_seeds.voice: short, blunt, and quiet, letting the silence do the talking: 'I held the line. You held the words. Now hold the weight.'
cast_seeds.breaking_point: walks away from the crown the moment you take the seal without offering him the sword's share of the rule
cast_seeds.name: Tamsin Holloway

cast_seeds.wants: to see the men he led out of the trench safe, even if that means following the con to the end
cast_seeds.holds: the loyalty of the handful of soldiers who serve you, and the bridge between your past and your future
cast_seeds.edge: follows you because you led men out of a trench, not because you sold him a kingdom, and watches the con with wary eyes
cast_seeds.tie: was saved by your bluff in the border campaign, and now guards your back while you talk
cast_seeds.voice: gruff, practical, and slightly amused by the absurdity of the situation: 'The mark wants a king. I want a man who can pay his men. Which one is in the room?'
cast_seeds.breaking_point: leaves the day you let the partner take the fall for the con, proving the old soldier's trust was worth more than the new king's crown
cast_seeds.name: Yestin Brightwater

cast_seeds.wants: to deliver the council's word accurately, without being caught in the middle of the con
cast_seeds.holds: the knowledge of the council's demands and the location of the river fords
cast_seeds.edge: is curious about the two men who think they can buy a country, and reports back with more nuance than the council expects
cast_seeds.tie: serves the mark, and has watched you and the partner since the pine clearing
cast_seeds.voice: quick, observational, and slightly mocking: 'He's bleeding on the dirt. You're bleeding on the paper. Which one dries first?'
cast_seeds.name: Evrard Yarrow
